newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria bars France from wheat purchase - traders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria bars France from wheat purchase - traders.

text.p: Algeria has excluded France from talks to buy wheat in what French exporters described as possible evidence of new tensions over comments by France's prime minister, grain traders said on Tuesday.

Algeria's official press agency accused Prime Minister Alain Juppe of interfering in its affairs after he called on Saturday for a "true democratic conscience" to be established in Algeria and said real democratic alternatives were currently lacking.

Private French exporters, usually leading candidates to sell wheat to Algeria with the help of French government credit, said they had been excluded from an international tender for 75,000 tonnes or three shiploads of wheat to be sent to Algeria by May.
"This is a political matter which is linked to what Juppe said," said a leading French exporter, adding that several firms had complained to France's Finance Ministry over the loss of sales.
Officials at the branch of the ministry which handles grain export credits, known as DREE, denied knowledge of the affair and declined further comment.

Algeria's reaction to Juppe's remarks recalled a similar row in February after France's foreign minister was reported as saying he hoped Algeria would hold elections under "open and incontestable conditions."

Algeria responded by telling Paris to keep out of its affairs, drawing a pledge from Foreign Minister Herve de Charette that France maintained a policy of non-interference in its violence-racked former colony.
Algeria launched its tender for the wheat purchase on Monday without specifying where the grain should come from, a common practice in the international grain trade.

In a previous tender this month, it invited offers from France, the United States and Argentina, three of the world's major suppliers. It has an outstanding French-backed credit line easing the cost of 60,000 tonnes of French wheat purchases.
